problems.q: Define matter in your own words.
problems.answer: Anything that has mass and takes up space

problems.q: Is color a physical property or a chemical property?
Is the ability to burn (flammability) a physical or chemical property?
Is salt water a pure substance or a mixture?
Name one example of a pure substance.
problems.answer: Pure water (or pure copper, pure gold)

problems.q: What does mass measure, and in what unit?
problems.answer: How much matter an object contains; grams

problems.q: Write the formula for density.
A rock has a mass of 60 g and a volume of 20 mL. Find its density.
Water has a density of 1 g/mL. Will an object with a density of 0.7 g/mL float or sink?
What tool is used to measure the mass of an object?
Is ice melting a physical change or a chemical change?
Is wood burning a physical change or a chemical change?
Name one sign that a chemical change has happened.
problems.answer: A color change, bubbles/gas, or heat/light (any one)

problems.q: In a physical change, does the substance stay the same or become new?
Is dissolving sugar in water a physical or chemical change?
In which state are particles packed tightly and only vibrate in place?
Which state takes the shape of its container but keeps its own volume?
Which state spreads out to fill its whole container?
Name the three common states of matter.
Are ice, liquid water, and water vapor different substances or the same substance?
What is the change from a solid to a liquid called?
What is the change from a liquid to a gas called?
What is the change from a gas to a liquid called?
What is the change from a liquid to a solid called?
During a change of state, does the substance become a new substance?
problems.answer: No; it stays the same substance

problems.q: If you squeeze a gas into a smaller space, what happens to its pressure?
What happens to gas particles when the gas is heated?
problems.answer: They move faster and spread out

problems.q: Why does a balloon shrink in cold air?
problems.answer: The gas cools, so the particles slow down and move closer together

problems.q: What causes the pressure of a gas?
problems.answer: Particles hitting the walls of the container

problems.q: Why does a balloon get bigger in a hot car?
problems.answer: The gas warms up and its particles spread out

problems.q: Define energy in your own words.
problems.answer: The ability to do work or cause change

problems.q: What is the energy of motion called?
What is the stored energy of position called?
Does a ball at the top of a hill have mostly kinetic or potential energy?
Of two cars with the same mass, which has more kinetic energy: the faster one or the slower one?
What form of energy is stored in food, fuel, and batteries?
What form of energy comes from moving particles and gives us heat?
What form of energy does a moving bicycle have?
What form of energy does a ringing bell produce?
Can energy change from one form to another?
What is it called when energy changes from one form into another?
State the Law of Conservation of Energy.
problems.answer: Energy is never created or destroyed; it only changes form

problems.q: A flashlight changes chemical energy into mainly what form?
As a roller coaster speeds downhill, potential energy changes into what?
If a toy starts with 100 units of energy, how much total energy is there after it runs?
What does temperature measure?
problems.answer: How fast the particles in matter are moving

problems.q: In which direction does heat always flow?
problems.answer: From a warmer object to a cooler object

problems.q: What is thermal energy?
problems.answer: The total energy of all the moving particles in an object

problems.q: When does heat stop flowing between two objects?
problems.answer: When they reach the same temperature

problems.q: When you put ice in a warm drink, does heat flow into the ice or out of the ice?
Which type of heat transfer carries heat as rays through empty space?
Which type of heat transfer happens by direct touch?
Which type of heat transfer happens in flowing liquids and gases?
How does the Sun's heat reach Earth?
Hot water rising and cool water sinking in a pot is an example of what?
What is a material that lets heat flow through it quickly called?
What is a material that slows the flow of heat called?
Are metals usually conductors or insulators?
Name one good insulator.
To keep a cold drink cold longer, should you use a conductor cup or an insulator cup?
Name Earth's layers in order from the surface to the center.
Which layer do we live on?
What is Earth's core made mostly of?
As you go deeper into Earth, does it get hotter or colder?
Which part of the core is liquid: the inner core or the outer core?
Which sphere includes all of Earth's liquid water?
Which sphere includes all the solid rock and land?
Which sphere includes all living things?
Which sphere is the layer of air around Earth?
Rain wearing down a rocky hill is an interaction between which two spheres?
What is the main source of energy for almost everything on Earth?
Which part of Earth gets the most direct sunlight?
Why are the poles colder than the equator?
problems.answer: Sunlight hits them at a slanted angle and spreads out

problems.q: Name one thing the Sun's uneven heating creates.
On a sunny day, which heats up faster: land or water?

6-1.title: The Atmosphere and Water in the Air

problems.q: What is the atmosphere?
problems.answer: The blanket of gases surrounding Earth

problems.q: What gas in the upper atmosphere blocks harmful ultraviolet rays?
What is humidity?
problems.answer: The amount of water vapor in the air

problems.q: How do clouds form?
problems.answer: Water vapor cools and condenses into tiny droplets

problems.q: What is the process of liquid water turning into water vapor called?

6-2.title: The Water Cycle and Weather Patterns

problems.q: What energy source drives the water cycle?
List the main steps of the water cycle in order.
Name two forms of precipitation.
problems.answer: Rain and snow (also sleet or hail)

problems.q: What is the step where water vapor forms clouds called?
Why is the water cycle called a 'cycle'?
problems.answer: Because the same water is recycled and the steps repeat

6-3.title: Air Masses, Fronts, and Predicting Weather

problems.q: What is a large body of air with similar temperature and moisture called?
What is the boundary where two air masses meet called?
What is the fast, high-altitude wind that steers weather called?
What do we call scientists who study and predict the weather?
Name two things meteorologists measure to predict weather.
problems.answer: Temperature and air pressure (also wind and humidity)

6-4.title: Severe Weather and Staying Safe in Florida

problems.q: Name one type of severe weather common in Florida.
Name one way to prepare for a hurricane.
problems.answer: Keep emergency supplies / board up windows / evacuate when told

problems.q: Name two things that protect your skin from harmful UV rays.
During a lightning storm, where is the safest place to be?
problems.answer: Indoors, away from windows and water

problems.q: Why do Floridians track storms closely?
problems.answer: To know when to prepare, evacuate, or take shelter

problems.q: What is a mineral?
problems.answer: A naturally formed solid with a specific chemical makeup and an orderly crystal pattern

problems.q: What is the color of a mineral's powder called?
What property describes how shiny or dull a mineral is?
Minerals are the building blocks of what?
If Mineral A can scratch Mineral B, which one is harder?
Name the three main types of rock.
Which rock type forms when melted rock cools and hardens?
Which rock type forms from pressed and cemented layers of sediment?
Which rock type forms when heat and pressure change a rock without melting it?
Marble forms from limestone changed by heat and pressure. What type of rock is marble?
What does the rock cycle describe?
problems.answer: How rocks slowly change from one type to another over time

problems.q: What process turns a rock into igneous rock?
What two forces turn a rock into metamorphic rock (without melting)?
What are the small pieces called that weathering breaks rock into?
About how long does the rock cycle usually take?
Which scientist proposed the idea of continental drift?
What was the single supercontinent that joined all continents called?
What is the idea that continents have slowly moved apart called?
Name one type of evidence for continental drift.
problems.answer: Matching fossils (also matching coastlines or rocks)

problems.q: Why do the coastlines of South America and Africa support continental drift?
problems.answer: They fit together like puzzle pieces

problems.q: What are the long underwater cracks where sea-floor spreading happens called?
What happens to hot melted rock at a mid-ocean ridge?
problems.answer: It rises, cools, and adds new rock to the sea floor

problems.q: Where is the youngest sea-floor rock found?
Is sea-floor rock far from the ridge younger or older than rock at the ridge?
What did sea-floor spreading help scientists explain?
What are the giant moving pieces of Earth's crust called?
What layer do tectonic plates float on?
About how fast do tectonic plates move?
What can form when two plates push together?
What often happens when plates slide past each other?
What is weathering?
problems.answer: The breaking of rock into smaller pieces

problems.q: What type of weathering breaks rock apart physically (like ice in a crack)?
What type of weathering dissolves or changes rock with water and acids?
Soil forms when weathered rock mixes with what?
Is water freezing in a crack and splitting a rock mechanical or chemical weathering?
What is erosion?
problems.answer: When broken pieces of rock and soil are carried away

problems.q: What is deposition?
problems.answer: When carried pieces are dropped in a new place

problems.q: Name two things that can cause erosion.
problems.answer: Wind and water (also ice or gravity)

problems.q: A river dropping sediment to build a delta is an example of what?
List weathering, erosion, and deposition in the correct order.
What is a landform?
problems.answer: A natural feature of Earth's surface

problems.q: Is Florida's land mostly flat and low or tall and mountainous?
Name one landform Florida does NOT have.
What force mainly carves out a river valley?
What type of landform is the Everglades?
What is the basic building block of all living things?
Name two features shared by all living things.
problems.answer: They use energy and are made of cells (also grow, respond, reproduce)

problems.q: What is another word for a living thing?
Is a rock a living thing?
About how many cells make up a human body?
What does it mean to classify living things?
problems.answer: To group them by shared characteristics

problems.q: Why do scientists classify living things?
problems.answer: To make them easier to study and compare

problems.q: How many parts does an organism's scientific name have?
What are the broadest groups used to sort all life called?
Why is a two-part scientific name useful?
problems.answer: It means the same thing to scientists everywhere

problems.q: What is an ecosystem?
problems.answer: All the living and nonliving things in an area working together

problems.q: Where does the energy in most ecosystems come from?
What are organisms that make their own food using sunlight called?
What does a food chain show?
problems.answer: How energy flows from one living thing to the next

problems.q: Is matter (like water and nutrients) recycled or destroyed in an ecosystem?

10-4.title: Microorganisms: Viruses, Bacteria, Protists, and Fungi

problems.q: What are living things too small to see without a microscope called?
Are bacteria single-celled or many-celled?
Which microorganism is not quite alive and must invade a cell to reproduce?
Name one group of microorganisms that includes mushrooms and mold.
Are all bacteria harmful?
problems.answer: No; some are helpful and some are harmful
